page: Amazon Web Services m5n.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server instance optimized for network and EBS workloads. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 82015.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 57124.09. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 4544.02 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 95.5 GB/sec. Database operations and key-value store performance are notable, as demonstrated by a PassMark database score of 21823.39 and Redis SET operations processing 77.84 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1334.0.

The lack of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware introduces specific architectural tradeoffs. While the server excels at high-throughput network tasks, static web serving at 48.53 GB/sec, and software compilation, it is poorly suited for large-scale LLM text generation, where it registers a low 5.26 tokens/sec on medium models. The hardware profile offers high resource density and balanced compute-to-memory allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for distributed database nodes, high-throughput web serving, container orchestration, and multi-threaded enterprise applications that require bare-metal access without virtualization overhead.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by a dedicated 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance is engineered for high-throughput networking, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. Benchmark results show strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and efficient database execution, with Redis SET operations reaching 77.84 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are average to poor. Given its bare-metal access and high network capacity, this server is suited for enterprise databases, multi-threaded applications, static web serving, and network-intensive workloads.
